Optimal.Notes: Medium textures and voxels give a noticeably better-looking world while shadows and AO remain off to protect frame rate. This profile holds well in early-game and modest bases but will dip in heavily-built areas.

profiles.Summary: Space Engineers is a demanding sandbox simulation that exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU class at recommended settings, but can run at reduced quality targeting 30 fps with careful tuning. No Deck-specific reports were found, so all profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparisons.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB reports with settings details were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs compared against the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (~GTX 1050 Ti class). On first launch, check fps in a new world with no builds, then in a medium-complexity base — if either dips below 25 fps, drop to the Max Battery profile and reduce Render Distance.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to ease GPU load; 8 W TDP and locked 30 fps keep the battery alive. In large or complex worlds, frame rate may still dip — reduce Render Distance further if needed.

KnownIssues: Marked 'Unsupported' on Steam Deck, likely due to lack of full controller support — keyboard/mouse or a custom controller layout may be needed.
The game is CPU-heavy in large worlds with many blocks; frame rate can degrade significantly as builds grow.
DirectX 11 title running under Proton may have occasional shader compilation stutters on first load.
Multiplayer sessions with many players/ships will likely be unplayable at Deck performance levels.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with uncapped TDP gives the best image quality the Deck can realistically sustain in open space or small bases; expect drops into the mid-20s in large grid-heavy scenes. Drop Render Distance or Model Quality immediately if the CPU becomes the bottleneck.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a 40 fps cap gives smooth, tear-free motion at a sustainable TDP; FSR at 1024x640 recovers enough GPU headroom for medium textures and models. CPU-heavy scenarios like large grids or busy multiplayer may still dip below 40 fps.

On your first session, check frame rate in an open-world area with a medium-complexity ship — if it drops below your cap consistently, drop to the Max Battery profile and reduce Render Distance further.
